Options and environment variables used by condathis

Source: R/condathis-options.R
condathis-options.Rd

condathis reads a small set of R options and environment variables to locate micromamba, choose a backend, and resolve its data directories. It also builds an isolated environment for every child process it spawns. That isolation clears or overrides many CONDA_* and MAMBA_* variables, so values set in the calling session never reach micromamba or the tools it runs.

This page leaves out fallbacks that apply only when the variables listed here are unset, such as HOMEDRIVE and HOMEPATH on Windows.

R options

Set these with base::options(), for example in an .Rprofile file.

condathis.micromamba_path

Character string. Path to a micromamba binary to use instead of the one managed by condathis. It has the highest priority in the micromamba discovery order (see micromamba discovery). The binary must report a compatible version (2.8.1 or newer). Otherwise, condathis uses the next candidate. Default: NULL (unset).

condathis.backend_priority

Character vector. The order of the registered backends for method = "auto". A new environment goes to the first available backend in this order: in create_env(), and when run(), run_bin(), run_pipeline() or install_packages() create "condathis-env". list_envs() and get_install_dir() report the backends in this order. The vector sets an order, not an allowlist: registered backends missing from the vector come after the listed ones, in alphabetical order. condathis loads a backend package that it knows, such as "rattler" of rattlerthis, when the vector lists the backend and a new environment needs a backend. The vector therefore applies even when nothing else loaded the package. Other names that are not registered are ignored. A value that is not a character vector without NA warns once per session with class condathis_invalid_backend_priority_option and is ignored. Default: "micromamba", so loading another backend package does not change where condathis creates new environments. An existing environment always uses the backend that owns it.

timeout

Numeric. Base R download timeout in seconds. While install_micromamba() downloads the binary, condathis uses the larger of this value and the timeout argument as the limit for each download. The limit applies to both curl and utils::download.file(). Inf, or 0 when both values are 0, means no limit. condathis lowers a finite limit above 2147483 seconds (about 24.8 days) to that value, because older libcurl versions reject larger values. condathis ignores a session value that is not a single, non-negative number. It restores the session value afterwards.

For example, this call in an .Rprofile file uses a specific micromamba binary, and creates new environments with the "rattler" backend when the rattlerthis package is installed (micromamba stays the fallback):

options(
  condathis.micromamba_path = "/opt/micromamba/bin/micromamba",
  condathis.backend_priority = c("rattler", "micromamba")
)

Environment variables read by condathis

Set these in the shell, in an .Renviron file, or with base::Sys.setenv().

CONDATHIS_MICROMAMBA_PATH

Path to a micromamba binary. Same effect as the condathis.micromamba_path option, with lower priority than that option.

CONDA_PREFIX

Prefix of the Conda environment active in the calling shell. condathis reads it to look for micromamba inside that prefix during discovery, and to remove the activation of the R session from child processes (see The activation of the R session below). It never passes it on to child processes.

PATH

Searched for micromamba as the last discovery fallback. Also the base PATH of child processes, without the binary directories of the Conda and pixi environments that the R session runs in (see below). run(), run_bin() and run_pipeline() put the environment's binary directories in front of it.

PATHEXT

Windows only. Extensions tried when a command name is resolved inside an environment. Default when unset: .COM;.EXE;.BAT;.CMD.

TAR

A system tar program, as used by base R: a program name, looked up on PATH, or the path of an executable file. install_micromamba() extracts the micromamba archive with R's internal tar, and uses this program only when that fails. It skips the value internal, an empty value, and a program that cannot be found or run, and uses tar on PATH instead. TAR does not support arguments.

For example, this line of an .Renviron file names the same micromamba binary as the option above:

CONDATHIS_MICROMAMBA_PATH=/opt/micromamba/bin/micromamba

Environment variables that set data and cache directories

condathis keeps micromamba, its environments and its package cache in the condathis data directory, tools::R_user_dir("condathis", "data") (see get_install_dir()). Every other backend keeps its environments and caches in a directory of its name inside it, such as R/condathis/rattler (see backend_root_dir()). These variables move those directories through the rules of tools::R_user_dir(). Backends have no options or environment variables of their own for them.

R_USER_DATA_DIR

Base data directory. Takes precedence over XDG_DATA_HOME. The condathis data directory is its R/condathis subdirectory.

XDG_DATA_HOME

Base data directory when R_USER_DATA_DIR is unset. On macOS, when both are unset, condathis uses ~/.local/share instead of the platform default. That default is under ~/Library/Application Support, which contains a space, and micromamba run can fail on paths with spaces.

R_USER_CACHE_DIR, XDG_CACHE_HOME

Base cache directory, in that order. clean_cache() empties its R/condathis subdirectory.

HOME, USERPROFILE, APPDATA, LOCALAPPDATA

Home and application data directories. tools::R_user_dir() uses them when none of the variables above is set: on Windows, APPDATA for the data directory and LOCALAPPDATA for the cache directory.

condathis creates the condathis data directory only when a call needs it. Queries, such as list_envs(), env_exists(), list_packages() and validate_env(), create no environment and never install micromamba. get_install_dir() and get_env_dir() create only the data directory.

with_sandbox_dir() sets all the data and cache variables above to temporary directories. Environments, packages and the micromamba binary that condathis installs inside it, with every backend, then stay out of your own directories.

Environment variables for downloads

install_micromamba() downloads with curl::curl_download() when curl 5.0.0 or later is installed, and with utils::download.file() otherwise. Both honor the standard proxy variables, such as http_proxy, https_proxy, and no_proxy.

The processes that condathis starts, micromamba included, inherit these variables from the R session, so micromamba downloads packages through the same proxy. It ignores the proxy settings of your .condarc and .mambarc files (see CONDARC below).

These variables also reach every process unchanged, on purpose:

Certificates

SSL_CERT_FILE, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, PIP_CERT and the other certificate variables of the tools that a process runs.

Package indexes and credentials of pip and uv

Such as PIP_INDEX_URL, PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL, PIP_CONFIG_FILE (except for micromamba list, see below), UV_INDEX_URL and NETRC. micromamba create installs the pip: section of an environment file with them.

CONDA_OVERRIDE_*

Such as CONDA_OVERRIDE_CUDA, CONDA_OVERRIDE_GLIBC and CONDA_OVERRIDE_OSX. They set the virtual packages (__cuda, __glibc, __osx) that micromamba solves for, also with --no-env. For example, CONDA_OVERRIDE_CUDA = "12.4" gets the CUDA builds of packages on a machine without a GPU.

Environment variables set or cleared in child processes

Every process condathis starts, whether micromamba itself or a command run by run(), run_bin() or run_pipeline(), starts from a copy of the calling session's environment, without the activation of the R session (see The activation of the R session below). condathis then applies the overrides below to that copy only. condathis never modifies the calling R session. A process that you start yourself does not get these overrides. Pass --no-rc and --no-env to micromamba or conda to ignore your own Conda settings.

Cleared or reset, so that the user's own Conda or Mamba setup does not interfere:

CONDARC, MAMBARC

Set to "". With the micromamba backend, condathis also calls micromamba with --no-env and with --rc-file pointing at condathis-micromamba.yaml in the condathis data directory. So micromamba ignores the user's configuration files and MAMBA_* settings. That file pins pkgs_dirs to the condathis package cache, and sets shortcuts: false, so that micromamba adds no Start Menu shortcuts on Windows. One exception: micromamba extracts packages in subprocesses (micromamba package extract) that it starts without these options. These subprocesses still read the user's configuration files, such as ~/.condarc, ~/.mambarc and those in XDG_CONFIG_HOME. They also read the MAMBA_* variables that are not listed here.

CONDA_ROOT_PREFIX, MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX

Set to "" for every command of an environment, also when the activation of the micromamba backend sets MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX, as it does on Windows. micromamba itself gets the condathis data directory as its root prefix, with -r and in MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX. Without MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX, micromamba (2.8.1 to 2.10.0 checked) refuses to start, even for --version, when its default root prefix exists but is not a Conda environment. The default root prefix is $XDG_DATA_HOME/mamba, else ~/.local/share/mamba, on Windows else mamba in the roaming application data folder.

CONDA_PREFIX, MAMBA_PREFIX

Set to "".

CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV, MAMBA_DEFAULT_ENV

Set to "".

CONDA_PROMPT_MODIFIER, MAMBA_PROMPT_MODIFIER

Set to "".

CONDA_SHLVL, MAMBA_SHLVL

Set to "0". The commands of run(), run_bin() and run_pipeline() get "1" (see below).

CONDA_PKGS_DIRS, MAMBA_PKGS_DIRS

For micromamba and the commands of its environments, environments given by env_path() included: the pkgs/ directory of the condathis data directory. Packages are cached only there. The user's own ~/.mamba/pkgs cache is never read or written, and clean_cache() never cleans it. For the commands of other backends' environments: the directory conda-pkgs/ next to the envs/ directory that holds the environment, in the backend's data directory. A Conda tool run in such an environment caches its packages there, and clean_cache() empties it. It is "" when the environment is not in a directory named envs. An environment given by env_path() that such a backend runs gets the backend's own conda-pkgs/, not one next to the environment. With activate = TRUE, the activation of such a backend can set another value (see register_backend()).

MAMBA_ENVS_PATH, MAMBA_ENVS_DIRS

Set to "".

CONDA_ENVS_DIRS

Removed from the child environment.

CONDA_ENVS_PATH

For micromamba and the commands of its environments, environments given by env_path() included: the envs/ directory of the condathis data directory. For the commands of other backends' environments: the parent directory of the environment, and for an environment given by env_path(), the backend's own envs/ directory. The value is the same with activate = TRUE and activate = FALSE. With activation, the backend can set another value.

R_HOME

Removed, with every other R_* variable (see The startup of R below), so an R installed in a Conda environment does not pick up the R installation of the calling session.

TMPDIR

Set to a new temporary directory for each call. condathis removes it when the call returns.

TMP

On Windows, for every micromamba command: a directory in its TMPDIR. micromamba writes its temporary files there, such as the batch files of micromamba run, so they are removed with that directory, also when the command is stopped. The activate.d scripts see this value while the activation is recorded. A value that they build from it names the session's TMP, unless they wrote something in that directory: then the value names that directory, which the command finds in its TMPDIR, and the activation is recorded again for every command. The commands of run(), run_bin() and run_pipeline() keep the session's value, unless an activate.d script sets one. TEMP is never changed.

XDG_CACHE_HOME

For every micromamba command: the cache/ directory of the condathis data directory. There micromamba keeps its repodata cache, instead of in ~/.cache/conda, and the mamba/proc directory of micromamba run. The scripts that packages run when they are installed or removed see this value too. The activate.d scripts, while the activation is recorded, and the commands of run(), run_bin() and run_pipeline() keep the session's value.

HOME (USERPROFILE on Windows)

For micromamba env list, micromamba env remove and, unless it needs your home directory, micromamba create: the home/ directory of the condathis data directory. So micromamba does not rewrite ~/.conda/environments.txt (see Details in get_install_dir()). The scripts that packages run when they are installed or removed by these commands see this value too. On Windows, micromamba looks there for the Start Menu shortcuts of the removed packages.

Python, pip and uv: the Python state of the R session never reaches a process of condathis. So the python of an environment finds only its own modules, and micromamba create installs the pip: section of an environment file into the environment, never elsewhere. For every process, micromamba itself and the commands of run(), run_bin() and run_pipeline(), with and without activation:

PYTHONHOME, PYTHONPATH, PYTHONUSERBASE, PYTHONSTARTUP

Removed. To give a command a PYTHONPATH, set it in the command, such as run("env", "PYTHONPATH=/my/modules", "python", "script.py") on Linux and macOS, or add the directory to sys.path in the script.

PYTHONNOUSERSITE

Set to "1": the user's site directory (~/.local/lib/python3.*, on Windows a Python directory in APPDATA) is not on sys.path.

UV_PYTHON, UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON, UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT

Removed, so uv uses the python of the environment.

PIP_USER, PIP_REQUIRE_VIRTUALENV

Set to "false", which overrides user and require-virtualenv in a pip configuration file; PIP_REQUIRE_VENV, an alias that pip also reads, is removed. Otherwise pip installed into the user's site directory, or failed: the user's site directory is off, and a Conda environment is not a virtual environment. So run("python", "-m", "pip", "install", ...) installs into the environment.

PIP_TARGET, PIP_PREFIX, PIP_ROOT

Removed, whatever their value. A target, prefix or root in a pip configuration file still applies (an environment variable cannot unset it). To install elsewhere, pass --target or --prefix to pip in the command.

An activated virtual environment of the session (VIRTUAL_ENV) is undone as well (see The activation of the R session below). The activation of the environment of a command comes after all this, so a variable that an activate.d script sets reaches the command.

For micromamba create and micromamba install, which run pip, or uv when the environment file lists it, for the pip: section, VIRTUAL_ENV and VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT are also removed, whatever their value.

For micromamba list, which list_packages() runs, and which runs python -m pip inspect in the environment: PIP_CONFIG_FILE is the null device (/dev/null, on Windows nul), so pip reads no configuration file, PIP_USER is "false", PIP_PATH and PIP_LOCAL are removed, and the working directory is a temporary directory, not the one of R. pip then reports only the packages of the environment.

Every other PIP_* and UV_* variable reaches pip and uv unchanged.

The activation of the R session. R can run in an activated Conda or pixi environment, or in several nested ones: R installed in a Conda environment, R started from a shell where conda activate or pixi shell ran, or R started through a pixi global binary. The processes that condathis starts do not get that activation, within the limits below. So a program of R's own environment does not run in place of one that the environment of the command lacks. Before the overrides above, condathis changes the copy of the session's environment this way:

PATH

The binary directories of these Conda prefixes are removed: the prefixes of CONDA_PREFIX, of every CONDA_PREFIX_<n> and CONDA_ENV_SHLVL_<n>_CONDA_PREFIX, and the prefix that R itself is installed in. Only a directory with a conda-meta directory counts as a prefix. Other entries stay, such as the condabin directory of conda init and ~/.pixi/bin. One exception on Windows: a command that is a program of R's own prefix, such as file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript.exe"), gets the binary directories of that prefix back at the end of its PATH, because it loads its DLLs from there.

CONDA_PREFIX_<n>, CONDA_ENV_SHLVL_<n>_*, CONDA_EXE, CONDA_PYTHON_EXE, _CE_CONDA, _CE_M, MAMBA_EXE

Removed. These variables record the activation of the session.

PIXI_PROJECT_*, PIXI_WORKSPACE_*, PIXI_ENVIRONMENT_*, PIXI_PROMPT, PIXI_IN_SHELL, PIXI_EXE

Removed. Other PIXI_* variables, such as PIXI_HOME, stay.

CONDA_BACKUP_<X>, <X>_CONDA_BACKUP, CONDA_ENV_SHLVL_<n>_<X>

The value of <X> before the activation, saved by the activation scripts of compiler and other packages, or by pixi. <X> gets that value back, as the deactivation scripts do: an empty backup of the first two forms removes <X>. The backups are removed.

Variables of conda-meta/state and etc/conda/env_vars.d

A variable that these files of the prefixes above set is removed when the session has exactly that value.

Variables of a pixi global binary

When one of the prefixes above is an environment of pixi global, a variable that its binaries set when they start is removed when the session has exactly that value. pixi records them in bin/trampoline_configuration of its home. R started through such a binary gets the whole activation of its environment, such as the compiler variables CC, CFLAGS and CONDA_BUILD_SYSROOT, and a compiler of the environment of a command would see them.

VIRTUAL_ENV, VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT

When VIRTUAL_ENV names a Python virtual environment (a directory with pyvenv.cfg), both are removed, and its bin directory (on Windows Scripts) leaves PATH. Activating a virtual environment sets them, and so does reticulate inside the R session when it uses one, also through Sys.setenv().

What reticulate changed for its python

When reticulate has started Python in the R session, the lib directories that it put in front of LD_LIBRARY_PATH on Linux (of its python and of the python a virtual environment was made from) are removed. For a python of a Conda environment, reticulate puts the binary directories of that environment in front of PATH; they are removed as those of the prefixes above.

Some changes cannot be undone. A value that an activate.d script of the session's environment set stays, unless it saved a backup above or a pixi global binary recorded it, and so does a PATH entry such a script added. For example, R installed in a Conda environment that has the compiler packages, and started from a shell where that environment was activated, passes CC, CFLAGS, CONDA_BUILD_SYSROOT and the other compiler variables of that environment to the processes it starts. The binary directory of an environment that no variable names any more stays too, such as the one of a pixi global binary that started the shell before another one replaced its CONDA_PREFIX. reticulate moves the directory of a python that is neither in a virtual nor in a Conda environment, such as /usr/bin, to the front of PATH; it stays there. On macOS, when /usr/local/opt/openblas exists, loading reticulate sets OPENBLAS and, when it is unset, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1; they stay too.

The startup of R. R also changes its own environment when it starts, and the processes that condathis starts do not get those changes either. So an R of the environment of the command never loads packages built for the R of the session, and a program of the environment never loads R's libraries or certificates:

R_*, _R_*

Removed, also a variable the user set, such as R_LIBS_USER or R_PROFILE_USER: only R reads them, and an R that the command starts sets its own. The R of the session keeps them.

EDITOR, PAGER, MAKE, SED, TAR, LN_S, CURL_CA_BUNDLE, MSYS2_ENV_CONV_EXCL

Removed when the session has exactly the value that R's startup gives them (etc/Renviron of R). A value the user set stays, such as EDITOR=nvim.

LD_LIBRARY_PATH, DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH, DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH

The directories that R put in front (etc/ldpaths of R) are removed. The directories after them stay.

PATH on Windows

The Rtools directories that R put in front (R_RTOOLS45_PATH) are removed. A command finds Rtools only when the PATH that R started with has it.

condathis learns the values of R's startup by starting R's own Rscript once per R session, without the user's .Renviron and .Rprofile. When that fails, only the R_* variables and the Rtools directories are removed.

With the default activate = TRUE of run(), run_bin() and run_pipeline(), condathis applies activation variables on top. For the micromamba backend, these are the variables that a real micromamba run activation sets. They include the variables from activate.d scripts shipped by the installed packages. These scripts run with the command's TMPDIR, user cache and working directory. condathis records the variables once per environment and R session. It reuses them until the environment (its packages, its activate.d scripts or env_vars.d files) or the session's environment variables change. It starts the command itself. Values that name the command's TMPDIR are recorded again for every command. Values that name the working directory are recorded again in another working directory. For other backends, the backend package sets the activation variables (see register_backend()). When the PATH of an activation names none of the environment's binary directories, condathis puts them in front of it.

In both modes and for every backend, a command of run(), run_bin() and run_pipeline() runs in exactly one activated environment, whatever the R session runs in: CONDA_SHLVL and MAMBA_SHLVL are "1", and CONDA_PROMPT_MODIFIER and MAMBA_PROMPT_MODIFIER are "", whatever the activation set.

With activate = FALSE, run(), run_bin() and run_pipeline() set this fixed set instead, without any backend code and without the activate.d scripts and env_vars.d files of the packages:

CONDA_PREFIX, CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV

The environment directory and its name. For an environment given by env_path(), the name is its directory.

CONDA_SHLVL, MAMBA_SHLVL

Set to "1".

CONDA_PROMPT_MODIFIER, MAMBA_PROMPT_MODIFIER

Set to "".

PATH

The environment's binary directories, in front of the PATH described above.

TMPDIR and CONDA_ENVS_PATH are the same as with activate = TRUE: they come from the clean variables above.

On Windows, variable names are matched case-insensitively. An override replaces any inherited spelling of the same name, such as Path.

micromamba discovery

condathis uses the first candidate that exists and reports a compatible version:

  1. The condathis.micromamba_path option.

  2. The CONDATHIS_MICROMAMBA_PATH environment variable.

  3. The binary managed by condathis, see micromamba_bin_path().

  4. A micromamba next to the running R, when R is installed in a Conda environment.

  5. A micromamba inside CONDA_PREFIX.

  6. A micromamba in the micromamba-env environment of the micromamba backend, in the envs directory of the condathis data directory. condathis ignores an environment of that name that another backend created.

  7. A micromamba on PATH.

A candidate that is a binary exposed by pixi global (a trampoline, with a trampoline_configuration/<name>.json file next to it) is replaced by the binary that it starts, the exe of that file, so the activation of the pixi environment that the trampoline sets never reaches micromamba. The option and the variable keep the value you set.

A compatible version is 2.8.1 or newer. When no candidate is compatible, the first function that needs micromamba calls install_micromamba(), which downloads the default version into the managed location. That function says so first, unless its verbose is "silent", with a message of class condathis_micromamba_downloading. Queries, such as list_envs(), never download it.

Interactive sessions

In interactive sessions, condathis shows spinners for every verbose level except "silent". A session is interactive when rlang::is_interactive() returns TRUE. install_micromamba() shows the progress of its download only in interactive sessions, and only when its verbose is "output" or "full". When another function installs micromamba because no usable binary was found, the progress shows only with verbose = "full". Set the rlang_interactive option to FALSE to turn spinners and progress off in an interactive session.

See also

get_install_dir(), micromamba_bin_path(), install_micromamba(), with_sandbox_dir(), tools::R_user_dir(), condathis-conditions

Examples

# Redirect all condathis data to temporary directories
condathis::with_sandbox_dir({
  print(condathis::get_install_dir()$path)
})
#> [1] "/tmp/Rtmpel16Et/condathis-sandbox-29a672d275/data/R/condathis"
